question: Which narrative details of the canon's primeval history are absent from Genesis but present in other ancient texts held in the project library, and which have no ancient parallel there?

status_codes.D: different content in the same slot
status_codes.-: episode not covered by the library holding

columns.QUR: quran (Arabic only; English glosses are the researcher's)

class_labels.shared-not-genesis: Shared with an older text, absent from or reversed in Genesis
class_labels.genesis-has-it: Already in Genesis (the canon's addition, if any, has no ancient counterpart)
class_labels.canon-contradicts-older: The canon contradicts the older texts
class_labels.unique-and-contradicted: Canon only, and contradicted by every text that covers the point
class_labels.unique: Canon only (no counterpart found in the library)

items.detail: Home-world public opinion and government forbid the life experiments; the scientists leave for a distant planet

canon.fr: l’opinion publique de notre planète et le gouvernement interdirent à ces savants de poursuivre leurs expériences

ATR.evidence: the making of man is approved by the whole assembly: '"Yes!" they answered in their assembly' (an-nu i-pu-lu i-na pu-uḫ-ri-šu-nu)

SUM.evidence: the gods themselves ask for the substitute to be made

items.detail: Earth is found, not made; it is water-covered; the 'light' is tested for harmful rays

canon.fr: Ils ont «créé», découvert en réalité, la terre
Il s’avéra que le soleil chauffait correctement la Terre sans lui envoyer de rayons nocifs

GEN.evidence: primeval waters are present ('the breath of the Elohim hovering over the face of the waters'); the Earth is not 'found'

BER.evidence: pre-existing 'darkness and an abyss of waters'; first creatures 'not being able to bear the prevalence of light, died'

items.note: Only the pre-existing water is shared, and Genesis has that too.

items.detail: One continent is raised from a shallow sea-bed by explosions; the continents later split (at the Flood, LWTE ch. 4)

canon.fr: fait en sorte que de la matière soit enlevée du fond des mers et qu’elle s’amasse au même endroit, ce qui forma un continent
les plaques continentales se séparèrent brutalement

items.canon_voice: Yahweh (TBWTT); Marcel Terrusse, guide (LWTE-4:40, see LWTE-4:95)

GEN.evidence: waters gathered 'to one place', dry ground appears; no explosions, no later break-up

items.detail: Several teams of makers work in parallel, meet, compare and hold contests

canon.fr: Ils se sont répandus sur cet immense continent en divers groupes de recherche scientifique
organisaient des concours pour désigner l’équipe de savants ayant créé l’animal le plus beau ou le plus intéressant
Chaque équipe se mit au travail, nous pûmes comparer bientôt nos créations

GEN.evidence: one grammatical subject; only the plural 'Let us make'

ATR.evidence: 'The womb-goddesses were assembled'; 'she nipped off fourteen pieces of clay' (14 ki-iṣ-ri ik-ta-ri-iṣ); 'seven and seven they fashioned: seven male'

SUM.evidence: an explicit making-contest between two makers: 'As for the form of mankind — whether it turns out fair or ill is in (my) hands' / 'I will counter-balance it' / 'let me, in turn, fashion (one) for you'

items.note: Contest between makers is in Enki and Ninmah; plural birth-goddesses and a plural first batch are in Atrahasis. No text has geographically separate teams.

items.detail: Some teams make monsters; earlier human 'prototypes' are superseded

canon.fr: d’autres équipes de savants créèrent des animaux épouvantables, des monstres
les crânes des premiers prototypes d’homme qui furent supplantés par d’autres plus évolués

GEN.evidence: 'the great dragons' (ha-tanninim ha-gedolim) are among the creatures; no failed or superseded makes

SUM.evidence: defective humans made in the contest; Umul: 'not a living man, is not a [dead] man — he cannot sustain himself'

BER.evidence: 'most hideous beings ... creatures in which were combined the limbs of every species of animals'; they die and 'other men and animals' are formed

items.detail: Earlier creation attempts fail (destroyed on order; burned by a star's harmful rays; choked by vegetation); two other planets seeded

canon.fr: deux nouveaux échecs dus l'un à la trop grande proximité d'un astre dont les rayons nocifs brûlèrent leur création
les Elohim ont créé également la vie sur deux autres planètes à cette époque

BER.evidence: a first creation that dies of the light, then a second 'capable of bearing the air'

items.note: Other planets: no parallel. The failed-first-creation shape has the Berossus partial only. The canon grounds the detail in Matthew 13, not in any primeval text.

items.detail: Man is made artificially, in laboratories, in the makers' image

canon.fr: voulurent créer un homme comme nous artificiellement
entièrement synthétiques dans les laboratoires de leur planète d'origine

GEN.evidence: image and likeness; formed 'dust from the ground' — the image motif is Genesis' own

ATR.evidence: substance not image: 'With the flesh of the god and (his) blood' ... 'so that god and man' / 'may be mixed together in the clay' (i-na ši-ir i-li ù da-mi ... i-lu-um-ma ù a-wi-lum)

SUM.evidence: 'having drawn out from his own mind the form of his own being'; 'the human whose form is mine'; 'he placed the first of humankind in the brick-mould'

BER.evidence: divine blood mixed with earth: 'On this account it is that they are rational, and partake of divine knowledge'

QUR.evidence: a mortal from clay (my gloss of the Arabic)

items.note: Laboratory, test-tube, chemicals: no ancient counterpart; every ancient text has clay/dust.

items.detail: Why man is made: the ablest makers want to make a being like themselves (no labor motive)

canon.fr: C’est alors que les plus habiles d’entre nous voulurent créer un homme comme nous artificiellement

GEN.evidence: to rule the animals; 'to work it and to guard it'

ATR.evidence: 'let man bear the labor of the gods' (a-wi-lum li-iš-ši du-ul-li i-li)

SUM.evidence: 'fashion a substitute for the gods (?), so that they may be released from their toil'; 'took them up to provide rations for the gods'

items.note: The canon's creation motive is the opposite of the Mesopotamian labor anthropogony (core 0034).

items.detail: Humans supply food to the makers: offerings prompted by the exiles; after the Flood Noah pledges a share of crops and herds 'for their subsistence'

canon.fr: poussèrent les hommes à leur amener de la nourriture
Noé s’engagea à verser une part de toutes les récoltes ou élevages aux créateurs pour leur subsistance

GEN.evidence: offerings exist; YHWH 'smelled the soothing aroma'; nothing about subsistence

ATR.evidence: without mankind 'The Anunna, the great gods, sat in thirst and hunger' (uš-bu i-na ṣú-mi ù bu-bu-ti); 'like flies they gathered over the offering'

GIL.evidence: 'The gods gathered like flies around the (lord-of-the-)sacrifice' (ilānu kīma zumbī eli bēl niqê ip-taḫ-ru)

SUM.evidence: people 'to provide rations for the gods' (diĝir-re-e-ne-ra šukur2-še3 mu-un-dab5-be2)

OTH.evidence: the Mekone division of the ox between gods and men

items.note: The makers' material dependence on human produce is a Mesopotamian idea that Genesis has reduced to an aroma. In the canon it is a post-exile and post-Flood arrangement, not the purpose of creation (D08).

items.detail: The home world objects to the making of man and fears he will surpass his makers; man must be kept ignorant

canon.fr: Ils craignaient que ces hommes soient un danger pour eux si leurs capacités ou leurs pouvoirs s’avéraient supérieurs à ceux de leurs créateurs
à la condition qu'ils ne créent pas d'êtres à leur image

GEN.evidence: divine alarm at human parity is in Genesis ('has become like one of us'; 'nothing will be withheld from them') but nobody objects to the creation itself

ATR.evidence: unanimous approval

SUM.evidence: Anu: 'Why did Ea reveal (the things) of heaven and earth to a son of humankind?'

JUB.evidence: Mastema: 'great is the wickedness of the sons of men'

QUR.evidence: the angels object before the creation: a-tajʿalu fīhā man yufsidu fīhā wa-yasfiku d-dimāʾ (“will you place in it one who will work corruption in it and shed blood?” — my gloss); Iblīs refuses to bow

OTH.evidence: Zeus 'would not give the might of unwearying fire' to mortal men

items.note: An objection from within the heavenly assembly, made before or at the creation of man, on the ground that man will be violent: Quran 2:30. Not in Genesis, not in Mesopotamia.

items.detail: Satan is one of the Elohim, head of the party that expects only evil from man; he is later licensed to test humans

canon.fr: l’un d’entre eux nommé Satan, fait partie de ceux qui ont toujours condamné la création d’autres êtres intelligents
Satan pensait qu'il ne fallait rien attendre de bon de ces créatures fabriquées en laboratoire
l'on confie à Satan le soin de tester les prophètes

GEN.evidence: no Satan in Genesis; the canon takes him from Job 1 (TBWTT-3:250)

ATR.evidence: Enlil is the god hostile to mankind, but he is the ruler, not an opposition

ENO.evidence: 'the violence of the Satans' (plural class)

JUB.evidence: Mastema, 'chief of the spirits', negotiates before God for licence over mankind; proposes the test of Abraham ('bid him offer him as a burnt-offering ... and Thou wilt know if he is faithful'); 'was put to shame'

QUR.evidence: Iblīs asks for and is granted respite and announces he will mislead them all (my gloss)

items.note: The licensed adversary who doubts man and tests him is Second Temple and Qur'anic. Jubilees puts the Satan-figure behind the Abraham test; the canon's own Abraham paragraph (TBWTT-2:89) names only 'les créateurs'.

items.detail: The makers teach the first man the names and properties of plants and animals

canon.fr: Les créateurs lui apprirent le nom et les pouvoirs de tout ce qui vivait autour de lui

GEN.evidence: the man does the naming: 'brought them to the human to see what he would call them'

BER.evidence: Oannes 'gave them an insight into letters and sciences ... made them distinguish the seeds of the earth'

JUB.evidence: 'we gave him work, and we taught him to do everything that was fitting to be done'

QUR.evidence: wa-ʿallama Ādama l-asmāʾa kullahā (“and He taught Adam the names, all of them” — my gloss)

items.note: The canon quotes Genesis 2:19 and then states the reverse of it; the reversal matches Quran 2:31 and, more loosely, Jubilees 3:15.

items.detail: The prohibition concerns scientific knowledge (books)

canon.fr: ne touche pas aux livres scientifiques sinon tu mourrais

GEN.evidence: tree of knowing good and bad

SUM.evidence: 'Wisdom he gave him; eternal life he did not give him' (ne-me-qa id-din-šu napišta dāriti ul id-din-šu)

ENO.evidence: 'the tree of wisdom' (v. 6, inside library refId 1ENO-32:4)

items.note: Books: no ancient counterpart in the library (core 0072 records the Sendy parallel).

items.detail: The 'serpent' is a small group of the makers themselves who, out of love for the humans, tell them the truth

canon.fr: quelques-uns qui aimaient profondément leurs petits hommes
Le «serpent», ce petit groupe de créateurs qui avait voulu apprendre la vérité à Adam et Ève
révéler à ces êtres qu'ils ne sont pas des «dieux» mais des hommes comme eux

GEN.evidence: the serpent is 'shrewder than any wild animal of the field'; its statement is confirmed by 3:22

ATR.evidence: a member of the assembly sides with mankind against it: 'he kept thwarting the work of Enlil'; 'I did it, indeed, against your will!'

GIL.evidence: 'the secret of the gods he heard'

SUM.evidence: a god reveals 'heaven and earth' to a human and the high god objects

ENO.evidence: the tempter of Eve is one of the angels: Gâdreêl — 'he led astray Eve' (v. 6, inside library refId 1ENO-69:4); Asael 'revealed the mysteries of the age that are in heaven' — valued as sin

QUR.evidence: the tempter is Iblīs/the Shayṭān, a member of the heavenly assembly, not an animal — valued as enemy

OTH.evidence: 'kindly Prometheus' steals fire for men, deceiving Zeus (κλέψας ἀκαμάτοιο πυρὸς τηλέσκοπον αὐγήν)

items.note: Two separable features. (a) The tempter belongs to the heavenly company: 1 Enoch 69, Quran — negative valence. (b) A member of the divine company benefits mankind against the ruling decision: Ea, Prometheus — positive valence. The canon has (a)'s identity with (b)'s valence. No library text has both.

items.detail: The disclosing group is sentenced by the home government to live on Earth; the other makers must leave

canon.fr: était condamné par le gouvernement de la planète originelle à vivre sur Terre en exil tandis que les autres créateurs devaient stopper leurs expériences et quitter la Terre
Yahvé condamne les scientifiques qui ont désobéi à ses ordres à vivre en exil sur la Terre

GEN.evidence: 'on your belly you shall go' — an animal's curse

ENO.evidence: Watchers 'who have abandoned the high heaven' are bound 'in the valleys of the earth' (εἰς τὰς νάπας τῆς γῆς); the offence is the unions, not a disclosure in Eden

JUB.evidence: 'he removed them from all their stations; and he commanded us to bind them in the depths of the earth'

QUR.evidence: ihbiṭū ... wa-lakum fī l-arḍi mustaqarrun (“go down ... on the earth you shall have a dwelling for a time” — my gloss), plural address after the tempter's act

OTH.evidence: Prometheus bound; Titans 'beneath the wide-wayed earth ... no way out'

items.note: Confinement to the Earth of a heavenly group is Enochic; in Enoch it is imprisonment under the earth with no return, in the canon residence on it with later pardon (D39).

items.detail: Longevity is a technique ('tree of life'); the exiles obtain it for the chiefs of the first humans, hence the patriarchs' ages; it is not hereditary

canon.fr: Ils obtinrent ainsi qu’on fasse bénéficier les chefs de ces premiers hommes de «l’arbre de vie»
La longévité n’est pas héréditaire

GEN.evidence: the tree of life is barred to man; the long lives are stated without cause; the 120-year limit is present

GIL.evidence: godlike life is conferred on one man by decision of the gods; a plant is named 'The Old Man is Made Young!'

SUM.evidence: the huge spans belong to rulers: 'he ruled for 28800 years' (mu 28800 i3-ak); 'Life like (that of) a god they gave him'; Anu orders 'the food of life' for Adapa

BER.evidence: Xisuthrus 'translated to live with the gods'

ENO.evidence: the sons of the Watchers hope for long life: 'length of days shall not be theirs'

QUR.evidence: the tempter offers “the tree of immortality” (shajarat al-khuld — my gloss)

items.note: Longevity as something the gods can confer on selected men, and antediluvian longevity attached to rulers, are Mesopotamian. Genesis says the opposite about the tree.

items.detail: The 'sons of Elohim' who take human daughters are the exiled makers; the children are exceptional

canon.fr: Les créateurs en exil prirent aux hommes leurs filles les plus belles et en firent leurs femmes
en avoir des enfants exceptionnels

GEN.evidence: unions and 'the mighty ones who were from of old, men of name'; who the sons of the Elohim are is not said

ENO.evidence: a named, numbered group of Watchers, 'in all two hundred'; the offspring are giants who 'devoured mankind'

JUB.evidence: the Watchers first 'descended upon the earth ... that they might instruct the sons of men'; the offspring destroy one another

OTH.evidence: goddesses with mortal men 'bore children like to the gods'

items.note: Genesis has the unions. What the canon adds — the fathers are a specific group already under sentence on Earth — is the Enochic identification with the order reversed: in Enoch the union is the offence and the sentence follows; in the canon the sentence comes first. The canon values the children positively, Enoch and Jubilees negatively.

items.detail: The exiles' sons hand weapons to human women; men slaughter each other with them; this bloodshed is the case for destruction

canon.fr: avec les armes qui leur sont données par les fils des Elohim bannis, du groupe de Lucifer
qui parviennent à se faire remettre par eux des armes en échange de leurs charmes

GEN.evidence: 'the land was filled with violence' with no source named; metal cutting-tools come from a human, Tuval-Cain

ENO.evidence: 'Asael taught men to make swords and knives and shields and breastplates' (ואסאל אלף לאנשא למעבד סיפין וסכינין); Gâdreêl showed 'all the weapons of death to the children of men' (v. 6, inside refId 1ENO-69:4); a sword is handed to the giants (v. 2, inside 1ENO-88:1); knowledge passes through the wives ('this you made known to the women'); 'much blood that was shed upon the earth'

items.note: The closest single match in the register, and it is in the 1979 book only. 1 Enoch 69:6 gives one figure both roles the canon gives the Lucifer group: leading Eve astray and arming mankind.

items.detail: An accuser lays the evidence before the Council; the president decides

canon.fr: Devant les preuves ramenées par Satan devant le conseil des Eternels d'un tel carnage, Yahvé décide de faire ce que demande Satan

GEN.evidence: YHWH sees for himself

ATR.evidence: Enlil 'convened his assembly'; 'Anu and Enlil made all the gods swear'

GIL.evidence: 'the great gods' hearts were moved to bring on a flood. Their father Anu bound them by oath'

SUM.evidence: 'the word of the [assembly cannot be revoked]' (restored)

ENO.evidence: four heavenly beings bring the case — bloodshed, the unions, the revealed mysteries — before the Most High, who then rules

items.note: Assembly decision: Mesopotamian (already in core 0010). Accusation-then-ruling before a presiding figure: 1 Enoch 9–10, where the accusers are the loyal archangels, not a Satan.

items.detail: Why the destruction: (TBWTT) human scientific progress, the wish to equal the makers; (LWTE) human violence

canon.fr: Le progrès scientifique était énorme sur Terre et ils décidèrent de supprimer leur création
Le mal, c’est-à-dire le désir de devenir un peuple égal à ses créateurs, un peuple scientifique et indépendant
car il les juge dangereux en raison de leur violence

GEN.evidence: wickedness and violence — agrees with the LWTE motive, not the TBWTT one

ATR.evidence: noise of a multiplied humankind: 'The noise of humankind has grown burdensome to me' (ik-ta-ab-ta ri-gi-im a-wi-lu-ti)

ENO.evidence: knowledge motive: 'their ruin is accomplished because they have learnt all the secrets of the angels'; violence motive also present

items.note: The TBWTT motive (illicit knowledge) has one ancient counterpart in the library, 1 Enoch 65:6. The two canon books give different motives; the later one is the Genesis/Enoch violence motive.

items.detail: The decision is taken on the distant home planet

canon.fr: Ils décidèrent donc, de leur lointaine planète, de détruire toute vie sur la Terre en envoyant des missiles nucléaires

GEN.evidence: a decision by the deity; no place

ATR.evidence: 'Anu went up to the heavens'; the assembly

GIL.evidence: the gods who decide dwell in Shuruppak ('the gods (dwelt) within it', ilānu qerbu-šu) and flee 'up to the heaven of Anu' when it comes

ENO.evidence: the Most High, from heaven

items.note: Not a discriminating detail: every text puts the decision with the higher gods.

items.detail: The means: explosions; a tidal wave over the single continent; a sudden cataclysm, not prolonged rain; fallout afterwards

canon.fr: Le continent fut immergé par un immense raz-de-marée qui détruisit toute vie à sa surface
le déluge n'était pas le résultat d'une pluie continuelle comme on se le représente généralement

GEN.evidence: forty days of rain and 'all the fountains of the great deep burst open'

ATR.evidence: 'He shattered the land like a pot'; 'like a battle'; seven days

GIL.evidence: 'The Anunnaki raised up their torches; with their bright radiance they set the land ablaze' (ina nam-ri-ri-šu-nu uḫam-ma-ṭu mātu); 'The land was shattered like a pot'; 'Like a battle it came over the people'

SUM.evidence: storms 'stood together as one'; seven days and nights

ENO.evidence: 'the earth that it had sunk down'; 'shaken' (vv. 1, 3)

items.note: A short, violent, fire-accompanied, battle-like event is the Mesopotamian picture; missiles and fallout have no counterpart. The canon nevertheless keeps Genesis' 150 days (TBWTT-2:61), which the seven-day texts contradict.

items.detail: The survivor is warned by the dissident (exiled) makers, against the intent of those who decided — not by the destroyer

canon.fr: Mais les exilés, prévenus de la chose, avaient demandé à Noé de construire une fusée
Mais ces derniers apprennent que toute leur fantastique création va être détruite. Ils ne peuvent admettre cela

GEN.evidence: the destroyer himself warns and instructs: 'I am about to destroy them ... Make for yourself an ark'

ATR.evidence: Ea is under the oath and still warns: 'Dismantle the house, build a boat!' (ú-qú-ur bi-ta bi-ni e-le-ep-pa); 'I did it, indeed, against your will! I saw to it that life was preserved' (aš-šum na-ap-ša-tim uš-te-ṣi); 'Enki and Enlil have grown angry with each other'

GIL.evidence: 'Prince Ea was with them, bound by the (same) oath'; 'Who but Ea could (have) devise(d) this matter?'; 'I did not (myself) reveal the secret of the great gods'

SUM.evidence: 'Enki took counsel in his own heart'; the side-wall speech (speaker lost in the break)

BER.evidence: 'The deity Cronos appeared to him in a vision, and warned him' — one god, no dissent stated

ENO.evidence: the Most High sends the warning; the Watchers are the ones condemned

JUB.evidence: 'he commanded Noah to make for himself an ark'

items.note: The strongest item. The canon's structure (decision by one party, warning by another against it) is the Atrahasis/Gilgamesh structure and is the reverse of Genesis, 1 Enoch, Jubilees and the Quran. In the Mesopotamian texts the warner is a full member of the deciding assembly; in the canon he is a group already expelled from it.

items.detail: The exiles help build the vessel

canon.fr: Noé qu'ils aident à construire un vaisseau spatial

items.canon_voice: Raël (LWTE); TBWTT-2:58 has only 'avaient demandé à Noé de construire'

GEN.evidence: Noah builds

ATR.evidence: the man builds

ENO.evidence: 'the angels are making a wooden (building)' (v. 2, inside refId 1ENO-67:1) — loyal angels, on God's order

QUR.evidence: built “under our eyes and our inspiration” (bi-aʿyuninā wa-waḥyinā — my gloss)

items.detail: The vessel is a rocket that orbits the Earth; life is kept some thousands of kilometres up; 'above the earth and not on the waters'

canon.fr: une fusée qui devait tourner autour de la Terre durant le cataclysme
la vie était préservée à quelques milliers de kilomètres au-dessus de la Terre
il est bien dit qu’elle s’éleva audessus de la Terre et non pas sur les eaux
c'était le seul vaisseau... spatial

GEN.evidence: 7:17 has the quoted phrase with its cause — 'the waters increased and lifted up the ark, and it rose above the land' (וַתָּרָם מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ) — and 7:18 continues 'the ark went on the face of the waters' (וַתֵּלֶךְ הַתֵּבָה עַל־פְּנֵי הַמָּיִם); it grounds on Ararat

ATR.evidence: pitch; 'he cut the mooring-rope and set the boat adrift'

GIL.evidence: punt-poles; launched 'until two-thirds of her had entered the water'; 'On Mount Nimush the boat came to rest'

SUM.evidence: 'the great boat had been tossed by the destructive storms on the great waters'

BER.evidence: 'trust himself fearlessly to the deep'; stranded in Armenia, bitumen scraped off

ENO.evidence: 'a wooden (building)'; 'a great vessel ... covered in'

QUR.evidence: wa-hiya tajrī bihim fī mawjin ka-l-jibāl (“it ran with them amid waves like mountains”); “a thing of planks and nails” (my glosses)

items.note: No library text has a vessel that leaves the Earth; every one that describes it has a boat on water. The canon's proof-text is the first half of Genesis 7:17; the same verse names the waters as what lifts the ark and the next verse puts it on them. Loose congruences only: sealed and roofed 'like the Apsû, so that Shamash may not see within her' (ATRA-WOH-III:i.17–18); the destination 'To the Gods' (CAG-3:17); Enoch lifted to 'a tower raised high above the earth' to watch (1ENO-87:3).

items.detail: What is preserved is a living cell, male and female, of each species; the animals are re-created from them afterwards

canon.fr: il suffit d’avoir une cellule vivante de chaque espèce, mâle et femelle, pour reconstituer ensuite l’être tout entier
chaque animal fut recréé à partir de la cellule préservée dans l’arche
certaines espèces animales dont l'on conserve le code génétique

GEN.evidence: living animals, 'two of each'. Purpose clause: 'to keep seed alive' (לְחַיּוֹת זֶרַע)

ATR.evidence: flocks, cattle, birds, beasts

GIL.evidence: 'Bring aboard the seed of all living things into the boat' (šūli-ma zēr napšāti kalāma ana libbi eleppi) — and also the animals themselves

SUM.evidence: 'for preserving the small animals and the seed of humankind' (numun nam-lu2-ulu3)

ENO.evidence: 'there shall come forth from it the seed of life' (v. 2, inside refId 1ENO-67:1)

QUR.evidence: min kullin zawjayni thnayn (“of each, a pair, two” — my gloss)

OTH.evidence: the vara is stocked with taoxma ('seed') of men, cattle, plants and foods, in pairs (mithwaire) — Avestan only in the library; gloss mine, unverified

items.note: 'Seed' as the thing carried is a formula of the flood tradition (Gilgamesh XI 27, the Sumerian Flood Story, Vendidad 2) and survives in Genesis 7:3. The canon's 'cellule' reads that word biologically. Re-creation of whole animals from it: no counterpart.

items.detail: Aboard: Noah and one couple of each human race; each race is put back at its place of creation

canon.fr: Il y avait à l’intérieur outre Noé, un couple de chaque race humaine de la Terre
Chaque race humaine fut replacée en son lieu de création

GEN.evidence: Noah's household only; the nations descend from his sons

ATR.evidence: 'His family'

BER.evidence: 'his wife, his children, and his friends'

ENO.evidence: three with him

QUR.evidence: his household and the few who believed

items.detail: Noah was not believed and was mocked

canon.fr: Autrefois Noé ne fut pas cru et les gens se moquaient de lui quand il se préparait pour la destruction

ATR.evidence: he addresses the elders with a cover story

GIL.evidence: 'But what shall I answer' / '(when) the city, the populace, and the elders (ask me)?'

QUR.evidence: wa-kullamā marra ʿalayhi malaʾun min qawmihi sakhirū minhu (“whenever chiefs of his people passed by him they mocked him” — my gloss)

items.note: A small clean case: not in Genesis, explicit in Quran 11:38.

items.detail: Those who ordered the destruction learn only afterwards that life survived, and are alarmed

canon.fr: Ils observaient toujours la terre et s’étaient aperçus que la vie n’avait pas été détruite

GEN.evidence: 'The Elohim remembered Noah'

ATR.evidence: 'When Enlil saw the boat' / 'he was filled with fury at the Igigi' / 'Where did life escape?' (e-eš-ta uṣ-ṣí-a-am na-pí-iš-tum) / 'How did a man survive the catastrophe?'

GIL.evidence: 'Has anyone (here) come out alive? No man was to have survived the destruction!'

items.note: In the Mesopotamian texts the discovery is immediate, at the sacrifice; in TBWTT it comes at the Babel episode.

items.detail: The makers promise never again to destroy mankind; the reason

canon.fr: promirent de ne jamais essayer de les détruire à l’avenir, car ils avaient compris qu’il était normal qu’ils veuillent faire des progrès
C'est alors que les Elohim s'aperçoivent qu'ils ont été eux-mêmes créés de la même manière qu'ils ont créé les hommes
Ils décident alors que plus jamais ils n'essaieront de détruire l'humanité

GEN.evidence: 'I will not again strike down every living thing' — reason: 'the inclination of the heart of the human is evil from his youth'

ATR.evidence: reproach ('without deliberating'), and lesser instruments 'Instead of your bringing on a flood'

GIL.evidence: 'These days let me remember — for ever, let me not forget!'

SUM.evidence: an oath 'by the life of heaven and the life of earth'

ENO.evidence: 'I will not again send wrath and plague upon it'

items.note: The promise is Genesis'. Both canon reasons are the canon's own: 'progress is normal' re-glosses Genesis 8:21; the discovery that the Elohim were themselves made (LWTE) has no counterpart.

items.detail: The Elohim are themselves created beings (message in an automatic vessel from their own makers)

canon.fr: le message que contenait le vaisseau automatique en provenance du monde des créateurs des Elohim

OTH.evidence: typological only: gods are themselves generated (theogony) — births, not manufacture by an earlier civilisation

items.detail: Not every species is re-established after the Flood (the great reptiles are left out); geology and coastlines are rewritten

canon.fr: certaines, considérées comme monstrueuses ou nuisibles pour le maintien de l'équilibre écologique, ne furent pas réimplantées
ils retrouvèrent des continents complètement ravagés par les destructions, méconnaissables

GEN.evidence: 'Of every living thing'

GIL.evidence: '(the world had become) the edge of the sea'

BER.evidence: the monstrous first creatures do not survive into the second creation — at the creation, not the flood

ENO.evidence: the giants are destroyed

items.detail: The tower is a vehicle for reaching the makers' world, built by the most advanced people with the exiles' help

canon.fr: il entreprit bientôt de se lancer dans la conquête de l’espace, aidé par les créateurs exilés
Ils construisirent donc une immense fusée : la Tour de Babel

GEN.evidence: 'a tower with its top in the skies'; stated aim: a name, and not to be scattered

BER.evidence: the Sibyl: 'a large and lofty tower, that they might climb up into heaven'; 'when it approached the heaven'

JUB.evidence: 'Let us ascend by it into heaven' (wa-yəbēlu nəʿrəg bottu samāya)

items.note: Ascent into heaven as the stated purpose is explicit in Jubilees and the Sibylline fragment, only implied in Genesis. Divine helpers in the building: no text.

items.detail: The purpose is to obtain the exiles' pardon by showing mankind grateful and peaceful

canon.fr: Ces derniers voulaient que les hommes aillent sur la planète des créateurs afin d’obtenir leur pardon en montrant que les hommes étaient intelligents et scientifiques mais reconnaissants et pacifiques

GEN.evidence: 'let us make for ourselves a name'

BER.evidence: 'glorying in their own strength and size and despising the gods'

ENO.evidence: a different episode with the same shape: the condemned Watchers ask a man to carry 'a memorial of petition for them, that they might find forgiveness' before the Lord of heaven (ἵνα γένηται αὐτοῖς ἄφεσις); he is borne up into heaven; the answer is 'There shall be no peace for you'

items.note: No Babel text has a pardon motive; those that state a motive state defiance. The pardon-petition-carried-to-heaven shape exists in 1 Enoch 13–16, attached to the Watchers before the Flood, with the opposite outcome.

items.detail: The home world is alarmed, comes, removes the most learned and scatters them among peoples whose languages already differ, and destroys the equipment

canon.fr: Les gens de la planète eurent peur en apprenant la chose

les dispersèrent sur tout le continent, dans des peuplades primitives, dans des pays où aucun ne pouvait se faire comprendre car le langage y était différent et ils détruisirent les appareillages scientifiques

GEN.evidence: alarm and scattering present; the one language is itself confounded (the canon has languages that already differ); the building merely stops; Genesis 10:5 already has nations 'each by his tongue'

BER.evidence: destruction: 'the winds assisted the gods, and overthrew the work upon its contrivers'; the cuneiform fragment printed by Smith: 'he confounded their speech'

JUB.evidence: 'the Lord sent forth a great wind against the tower, and overthrew it upon the earth'; 'we descended with him'

items.note: Physical destruction of the structure is in Jubilees and the Berossus/Sibyl fragments, not in Genesis. The canon's pre-existing language diversity agrees with Genesis 10 against Genesis 11 and against all the Babel parallels.

items.detail: The exiles are then pardoned, return home and plead for mankind

canon.fr: Les créateurs exilés furent pardonnés et eurent le droit de revenir sur leur planète d’origine où ils plaidèrent la cause de leur magnifique création
en permettant à l'équipe de Lucifer de revenir sur la planète des Elohim en les amnistiant de leur condamnation à l'exil

items.canon_voice: Yahweh (TBWTT: after Babel); Raël (LWTE: amnesty offered before the Flood)

ATR.evidence: Enki is never expelled; he answers for himself in the assembly

ENO.evidence: 'There shall be no peace for them upon the earth, nor any forgiveness of sins'

JUB.evidence: 'bound there until the day of the great judgment'

OTH.evidence: 'For them there is no way out'

items.note: Every tradition that has a confined heavenly group denies it release. The two canon books date the amnesty differently.

items.detail: Three roles: the one who presses for destruction (Satan), the president who decides (Yahweh), the faction that saves (Lucifer's group); Yahweh is also one of the makers

canon.fr: Je suis l’un de ceux qui ont créé la vie sur la Terre
Yahvé décide de faire ce que demande Satan
désobéissant aux ordres de Yahvé, le président du conseil des Eternels

GEN.evidence: one subject decides, warns, saves and promises

ATR.evidence: Anu the king who administers the oath; Enlil who proposes the flood; Enki who preserves life

GIL.evidence: 'Their father Anu bound them by oath, their counsellor — the warrior Enlil ... Prince Ea was with them'

ENO.evidence: accusers, judge; no saving faction

items.note: A role-structure observation only. It is not a per-figure identification, which core 0002 and 0008 exclude. In Mesopotamia the maker of man (Enki) and the destroyer (Enlil) are different gods; in LWTE the destroyer-president is himself a maker (TBWTT-2:24).
